item.title: Rainmatter Originals - Turning wastewater into a resource
item.description: Recently, I wrote about how serious our water problem is getting. This year’s weak monsoon has made it worse, and in Bengaluru, for example, that means dry borewells and expensive tankers. But we’re also wasting water we’ve already cleaned. Large apartments have to treat their own sewage, but only 20–30% of that water gets used. The rest goes down the drain. Meanwhile, IT parks and factories a few kilometers away are buying tanker water for their cooling towers.

item.title: Planting trees is not enough if they aren’t native
item.description: When we discuss rewilding and land restoration, ensuring that native trees are used is equally important. I wasn’t aware of this when I planted Conocarpus trees at home almost 10 years ago. No birds or animals have ever come to the tree. I also realised much later that these trees aren’t good for humans either. They cause allergic reactions in many people. It’s been so many years now that I feel bad about cutting them down, but maybe I should.
